title: CNSS matched workspace-accessibility causal control
objective: Test whether a shared, independently verified workspace with explicit bit-coordinate geometry improves Skill D acquisition relative to the recovered nonlinear workspace under the same adapter, optimizer, data support and evaluation protocol.
hypothesis: The original frozen workspace makes modular addition less computationally accessible to the registered low-rank adapter than the same operation represented in a shared signed-bit coordinate workspace.

arms.alternative: Deterministic 256-wide signed-bit coordinate workspace with eight groups of 32 repeated coordinates, amplitude 0.8, and a fixed group-mean decoder

alternative_workspace.construction: For each 8-bit state, encode each bit as -0.8 or +0.8 and repeat it over a disjoint group of 32 coordinates. Decode each bit from its group mean with a fixed positive logit scale.
alternative_workspace.interface_contract: same 256-dimensional state width and eight-bit output semantics as the original workspace

held_constant: rank-32 adapter architecture and parameter count
paired persisted step-zero adapter and optimizer states
same validation and fixed 64-state test partition
preflight_requirements: both workspaces reconstruct every 8-bit state exactly
alternative construction is independent of D and sealed test outputs
both workspaces have the same 256-dimensional interface
paired step-zero adapter checkpoints are finite and hash-verified
training candidate support and fixed evaluation partitions are unchanged
alternative workspace artifact is content-addressed and independently reloadable
no GPU or partner rerun authorization
primary_measurements: training, validation and held-out exact accuracy
paired per-seed delta versus the original workspace
latent displacement and affine accessibility diagnostics

success_gate.individual_d_gate: Each arm must be evaluated against the existing 95% held-out D competence threshold; the alternative does not unlock partner evaluation automatically.
success_gate.decisive_workspace_support: Alternative workspace reaches at least 95% held-out accuracy for all three seeds, improves the paired mean by at least 10 percentage points, and no seed is worse than the original workspace.
success_gate.partial_workspace_support: Alternative workspace improves paired mean held-out accuracy but does not meet the decisive criterion.
success_gate.null_or_negative: No paired mean improvement or a negative paired mean does not support the workspace-accessibility hypothesis under this construction.

interpretation_rule: A difference between workspaces would support a representation-accessibility effect only under the matched protocol; it would not establish that the signed-bit workspace is a general solution, that geometry alone is causal, or that CNSS composes across skills.
